name: Simon the Zealot
title: One of the Twelve
tagline: Known only by his name in the lists, and the word that marks it.
story: One of the Twelve, called Simon the Canaanite by Matthew and Mark and Simon Zelotes by Luke and Acts; nothing he said or did is recorded.

entries.title: Never named again
entries.text: The last verse that names him is Acts 1:13. After that Acts speaks of “the eleven” and “the twelve” as a body (Acts 2:14; 6:2) but never names him again.

verses.text: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;
Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

accounts.title: Chosen as one of the Twelve

verses.text: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.
And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
¶ And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

identifications.text: “Canaanite” here is explained not as a man from Canaan but as the Aramaic word for “zealot”, which Luke gives in Greek as Zelotes (Smith, 1884; Easton, 1897; Heidel, ISBE 1915). The Revised Version of 1881 prints “Cananaean”.
The same writers take the name to mean that he had belonged to the party of the Zealots, whom Josephus describes as fighting Roman rule. Scripture does not say so.
The Greek texts spell the word differently: the Textus Receptus behind the KJV has Kananitēs; Tischendorf's text has Kananaios.

scripture.text: Scripture does not mention him after Acts 1:13 and records nothing of his death.

items.q: Is Simon the Zealot the same man as Simon the Lord's brother, or Symeon son of Clopas?
items.full: Is Simon the Zealot the same man as Simon the Lord's brother, or Symeon son of Clopas? (Earliest source first.)

views.label: Different men
views.holders: Hegesippus (about AD 170) and Eusebius (about AD 325), who never call Symeon an apostle; A. C. McGiffert (1890)

argument.text: Hegesippus tells of Symeon son of Clopas, second bishop of Jerusalem, martyred under Trajan “at the age of one hundred and twenty years”; Eusebius, retelling it, says he “suffered a death similar to that of our Lord”, and calls him “a cousin, as they say, of the Saviour”. Neither calls him one of the Twelve. McGiffert holds that the Lord's brothers were not apostles, since they did not believe in him.

views.label: A kinsman of the Lord
views.holders: Jacobus de Voragine, The Golden Legend (about 1260); noted by C. M. Kerr (ISBE, 1915)

argument.text: The Golden Legend makes Simon and Jude brothers of James the Less and sons of “Mary Cleophas”; Kerr notes that Simon “has been identified with Simon the brother of Jesus”.

views.label: Nathanael
views.holders: C. M. Kerr (ISBE, 1915), drawing on Ethiopic texts translated by Budge

argument.text: Kerr argues that Simon may be Nathanael, citing an Ethiopic “Preaching of Simon, son of Cleopas”, whose heading calls him “Judas, which is interpreted Nathanael”.
